issues.legal_issue: A single lease naming multiple tenants together and fixing one aggregate rent establishes a composite tenancy, and an eviction judgment may be entered on admissions when the material facts establishing entitlement to possession are undisputed.
material_facts: The undisputed lease named all four tenants together and let the premises to them for one aggregate monthly rent, rather than separate individual rents.
The aggregate rent was increased above the amount at which the rent-control statute applied, after notice of the increase was served.
The landlord-tenant relationship and service of the notice terminating the tenancy were not disputed.

The tenants claimed they held separate tenancies and relied on correspondence, but the court found that it did not alter the character of the tenancy shown by the lease; rent was also tendered on behalf of all four tenants.
The landlord applied for judgment on admissions in the eviction suit. The trial court declined to decide the application before evidence, but the High Court granted an eviction decree.
issues.conclusion: The tenancy was joint and composite, not a set of separate individual tenancies. The undisputed admissions and lease established the material facts for eviction, so the High Court was justified in granting judgment on admissions; the special leave petition was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Order XII Rule 6 of the Code of Civil Procedure permits judgment on admissions in pleadings or otherwise, including admissions inferable from undisputed facts, to secure speedy judgment on the relief established by those admissions. The Court relied on Uttam Singh Duggal & Co. Ltd. v. United Bank of India, (2000) 7 SCC 120, and held that the lease was the primary document and that an isolated letter did not displace its terms. The rent increases were made under Sections 6A and 8 of the Delhi Rent Control Act, 1958; because the aggregate rent exceeded the Act's threshold, its protection did not apply. The notice terminating the tenancy was served under Section 106 of the Transfer of Property Act.

rule.if: eviction_suit_seeking_possession and lease_execution_and_contents_undisputed and lease_names_tenants_jointly and lease_sets_one_aggregate_rent and landlord_tenant_relationship_admitted and aggregate_rent_exceeds_rent_protection_limit and termination_notice_served

predicates.eviction_suit_seeking_possession: The claimant brought a suit seeking possession of rented premises.
predicates.lease_execution_and_contents_undisputed: The parties did not dispute that the lease was executed or what it said.
predicates.lease_names_tenants_jointly: The lease named the multiple occupants together as tenants.
predicates.lease_sets_one_aggregate_rent: The lease fixed one total rent for the premises rather than separate rents for each tenant.
predicates.landlord_tenant_relationship_admitted: The tenants admitted that the claimant was their landlord and they were tenants.
predicates.aggregate_rent_exceeds_rent_protection_l: The aggregate rent for the premises exceeded the level at which rent-control protection applied.
predicates.termination_notice_served: The landlord served notice terminating the tenancy.

issues.definition: When an eviction suit seeks possession and the undisputed lease and admissions establish a joint tenancy, a single aggregate rent above the protection limit, and service of a termination notice, judgment for possession may be entered on those admissions.
